# Question answer: generator-shortcuts

The strongest plausible shortcut is:

> For each color that occurs exactly twice in a row, fill between those two occurrences, even when a third nonzero cell of another color is also present.

That shortcut matches all five canonical demonstrations because every changed canonical row contains only the clean same-color pair and every unchanged row is blank. It differs from the selected rule because the selected rule first requires the row to contain **exactly two total nonzero cells**.

A concrete generated counterexample is seed `717`, sample index `2`, default difficulty:

```text
input
06000000006
06000040006
04000040000
80000000080
00000000000
00000000000
```

The intended output is:

```text
06666666666
06000040006
04444440000
88888888880
00000000000
00000000000
```

The second row is unchanged because it has three nonzero cells: two `6` endpoints and a `4` blocker. The shortcut instead returns this second row:

```text
06666666666
```

It fills the span for color `6` and overwrites the blocker.

I checked this in three independent ways:

1. The focused regression test evaluates every declared shortcut on all five canonical pairs and confirms this shortcut matches every canonical output.
2. The same test confirms that every three-demo generated window contains a case on which each shortcut disagrees with `rule_mirror`.
3. The strict semantic gate independently reports `ignore_blockers` as canonical-ambiguous and verifies that generated `blocked_pair` witnesses refute it, including `60/60` targeted rival checks. The Racket smoke stage also agrees with the Python mirror on `120/120` generated cases.

Yes, the proposed generator emits this case class deterministically: `schedule_profile` selects `blocked_pair` on every third sample. It therefore appears in every consecutive three-example lesson, not merely under a special override.
